findings.body: The new assertion hashes checkout bytes against LF-only digests. With Git for Windows' default `core.autocrlf=true`, these Markdown files are checked out with CRLF, so the test fails before exercising any installation. The Windows suite is enabled in `.github/workflows/forge-next.yml:23`, and `.gitattributes:1` only pins two unrelated JSON files. Moreover, `src/forge/sync.py:246` normalizes newlines when reading and line 146 writes UTF-8 bytes, so the new raw-byte `expected` comparison also disagrees with correct sync output on such checkouts. Preserve byte-exact assertions on generated files, but derive the baseline independently of checkout newline conversion. The default is confirmed by the [Git for Windows installer](https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/blob/main/installer/install.iss).

None is needed to implement the packaging assertions: the review contract already explicitly requires changing `tests/test_trim_skills.py`. Revert the plan, read-record and task-state changes to keep this branch within its authorized scope.
